verdicts.rationale: Drawing the link mark in the palette's value colour fixes the 1.39:1 mark on Paper. But the runtime injection Agent 1 showed (p4, currentColor) draws the frame in the VALUE colour, which is still a bright white frame on dark palettes. V02's own text says LABEL colour, which is quieter. At the host's DPR 1.5, a 1 px label-colour dashed frame still reads as dashes, and with a preset chosen it leaves the selection ring as the only 2 px frame. For a beginner, Default keeps three cues against its twin without hovering: the word, the link mark and the dashed frame. A link-blue glyph on a control that does not navigate was arguably a misleading cue anyway (INFERRED).

verdicts.rationale: In this panel the fill already means 'the saved choice' and the ring means 'the one you are pointing at'. The picker CSS says so (READ pi.css:1045-1057), and the 'On the dial now' picker directly above fills the on-dial row. Inverting the marks makes one colour mean two things on one screen. The selection also auto-resolves to the on-dial member, or else to the FIRST member (READ pi-common.js:393-404). When the on-dial reading is outside the set, the first member is selected with no click, so after an inversion the loudest mark would sit on a chip the person never chose and that is not on the dial: my round 1 B05 state. A visible caption naming the target does not fit beside the toolbar. X06's acceptance test requires human participants and cannot run in this campaign.
verdicts.regression_risk: Keeping the marks leaves X06's hypothesis untested. The ring is learnable by clicking (it moves under the click), but a beginner who never clicks could still read the filled chip as the toolbar's target. On open, the target is the on-dial chip itself, so the two coincide there.
verdicts.revised_correction: Keep fill = on dial and ring = selection. Defer any visible target caption until a layout exists that does not wrap the toolbar. Optionally re-test with people on the real host.
verdicts.acceptance_test: In dial-configured at 373 and 320, after clicking a non-current chip: the selected chip shows a 2 px inset ring at least 3:1 against its own fill, the selected and .current chips never share a background colour, and every toolbar button's aria-label names the selected reading. In the B05 state (on-dial reading not a member), no chip has the .current fill.
